result.title: Driving World Models Move the Camera, Not the Scene
result.summary: Plan-conditioned driving world models are used to compare candidate plans, so their forecast should change with the plan as the real scene would, yet widely used control metrics check only whether the camera follows the command. Recorded drives already contain real outcomes of plans that were never driven: retiming a log gives pose-matched images and LiDAR for other speeds, and a stereo rig records a laterally shifted view. Against these references, released world models move their camera but barely move the scene: their scene response, the share of the real change in distance that the forecast reproduces, reaches at most about a third of real video's, and the trajectory score cannot tell an executed speed command from an ignored one. Interventions inside the generator trace the failure to the plan's channel. The forecast geometry follows the context frames; once they carry the planned geometry, plan tokens add little. ReTime-Compose therefore delivers the plan as geometry, without training. It transports the frames of one logged-speed rollout to the planned cameras, and the frozen model completes only what no frame covers. Frozen generators then follow a 0.54 m lateral shift nearly as the real scene does on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and respond more than re-sampling to slow-down plans in three generators and to speed-up plans in two.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断 plan-conditioned 驾驶世界模型是否真让场景随计划改变，并借助重定时日志帧与立体位移构造反事实参考，指出计划通道贡献微弱、几何主要由上下文帧决定，进而提出无需训练的 ReTime-Compose 把计划作为几何输入。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用生成器内部干预定位「条件通道被上下文旁路」，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 是否真正影响推理状态而非被视觉上下文替代提供诊断模板，反事实参考的构造方式也或可供 latent 作用归因借鉴。
